meta.name: NOIR
meta.source_of_truth: derived by reading the repository source, not documentation
meta.summary: Three concurrent pipelines (vision, voice, web bridge) share one thread-safe RobotState on a laptop. All reasoning happens on the laptop; an ESP32 is a dumb actuator that executes single-character motor commands received over TCP. A Flutter app is a remote telemetry and control surface.

layers.name: Cognition & Voice
layers.purpose: Wake word to speech to intent to validated action tokens.

layers.name: Coordination & State
layers.purpose: Own the mode, serialise actions, supervise threads, survive failure.

layers.name: Transport & Bridges
layers.purpose: Reach the hardware and the phone. Every boundary is authenticated or allow-listed.

layers.name: Clients
layers.purpose: Telemetry, manual drive, camera view, push-to-talk.

layers.name: Hardware
layers.purpose: Execute motor commands. No decisions on the board.

components.name: RobotBrain
components.responsibility: Owns the CV loop at a 20 fps cap (LOOP_SLEEP_S = 0.05). Reads a frame, dispatches on RobotMode via match/case, emits one command char, sends it to the ESP32, pushes the frame to the web bridge, draws the HUD, handles hotkeys.
degradation: Camera missing -> CameraUnavailable caught, mode forced to IDLE, voice and manual still work
Web server start failure -> use_web disabled, loop continues
Voice pipeline start failure -> logged, loop continues
10 consecutive frame or loop errors -> clean shutdown with emergency S
components.notes: Frame pooling (deque maxlen=3) reuses same-shape numpy buffers instead of reallocating each iteration.

components.name: RobotState
components.responsibility: The single shared mutable object. Every field is a property guarded by one threading.RLock. Dict fields (imu, gps) return copy.deepcopy so no caller ever holds a mutable reference into shared state.
components.concurrency: touched by CV loop, voice pipeline, command queue, web bridge, state pusher

components.name: CommandQueue
components.responsibility: FIFO of validated action tokens drained by one executor thread. Serialises timed moves so two LLM actions never fight for the motors.
components.backpressure: Bounded at CMD_QUEUE_MAX (128). On overflow it evicts the oldest action, logs a warning, then retries the put. Never blocks a producer.
components.notes: A timed move flips mode to MANUAL for its duration to freeze the CV loop, then restores the previous mode.

components.name: ThreadSupervisor
components.responsibility: Polls registered threads every 1 s and restarts any that died. Each registrant supplies a factory returning a fresh Thread.
components.policy: MAX_RESTARTS 10 within a 60 s window, then the thread is marked degraded and left dead rather than crash-looping.

components.name: Startup health checks
components.responsibility: Non-raising probes run before the loop starts: Ollama /api/tags reachable, Piper binary present and executable, camera openable. Returns a dict; the caller decides abort vs degrade.

components.name: Typed config
components.responsibility: Single source of truth for every tunable, read from environment via typed helpers. validate_config() raises ConfigError at startup so the process dies early instead of failing deep inside a service. summary() emits a redacted snapshot for diagnostics.

components.name: HumanDetector (YOLOv8n)
components.responsibility: Person detection, COCO class 0 only, conf 0.45 / IoU 0.45. Degrades to disabled if ultralytics is not importable.
components.downstream: EMATracker smooths the bbox (alpha 0.25), then RobotComms.from_human_bbox converts geometry to a command.

components.name: HybridLineFollower (MobileNetV2)
components.responsibility: Fine-tuned MobileNetV2 classifier over 6 classes (Move Left, Move Right, No Line, Straight, Turn Left, Turn Right) mapped to a steer string. Weights load from a local path, else fall back to a HuggingFace download; if both fail it reports LOST rather than steering blind.
components.notes: The classic OpenCV scanline follower is present but commented out; the live path is ML-only despite the 'Hybrid' name.

components.name: GemmaVLAProcessor
components.responsibility: Vision-language-action. Sends a JPEG frame plus state context to Ollama and gets back {speech, actions} validated by the same Pydantic LLMResponse model as the text parser.
cost_control: Only fires when has_significant_change() sees MSE > 15 on 64x64 grayscale downsamples
Frame capped at 640 px long edge, JPEG quality 65
keep_alive 30m pins the model in GPU; a warm-up POST runs at construction to avoid the 20-40 s cold load
components.concurrency: inference runs on a throwaway daemon thread guarded by a busy flag, so the CV loop never blocks on the model

components.name: Camera geometry helpers
components.responsibility: compute_focal (cached), pixel_offset_to_angle, estimate_distance from known object height. HFOV 69 degrees.
components.distance_policy: bbox area > 40% of frame -> S (too close), |rotate| > 5 deg -> L/R, area < 15% -> F, else S

components.name: VoicePipeline
components.responsibility: One daemon thread running the whole conversation cycle so the CV loop is never blocked. Wake, transcribe, short-circuit, reason, speak, enqueue.
cycle: 0. Mint a 12-char correlation id and bind it to the log context
1. Wake word on phone audio queue, or a force_listen event from the app tap / spacebar PTT
2. Transcribe from phone queue if connected, else laptop mic
3. Regex CUSTOM_RESPONSES fast path - answered locally, no model call
4. Emergency keyword fast path - clears the queue, forces IDLE, never reaches the LLM
5. Snapshot RobotState so the model gets vision context
7. TTS speaks non-blocking, actions go to CommandQueue
components.warmup: Whisper and Piper load in parallel daemon threads at construction, saving 2-8 s on the first request.

components.name: WakeWordDetector
components.responsibility: 16 kHz PCM16 in 1280-sample frames. Triggers on instant peak or a 3-frame smoothed average at 80% of threshold. Works on the laptop mic or on variable-size chunks buffered from the phone queue.
components.discrepancy: README, CLAUDE.md and pyproject still name Porcupine / pvporcupine. The live code is openWakeWord. pvporcupine is a stale dependency.

components.name: WhisperSTT
components.engine: faster-whisper, CUDA with int8, automatic CPU fallback
components.responsibility: Energy-gated VAD recording then transcription. Waits up to no_speech_timeout for speech to start, then records until silence_timeout of continuous quiet, hard-capped at max_duration.
details: 5-chunk pre-roll buffer so the start of the sentence is not clipped
Phone threshold is auto-lowered to 40% of the laptop threshold (floor 150) for a different noise floor
Stale queued audio is drained before listening so a tap-to-talk starts clean
Silero VAD also runs inside Whisper on the recorded buffer

components.name: LLMParser
components.responsibility: Prompt with live state, force JSON output, then validate hard. Nothing unvalidated reaches the queue.
components.resilience: Exponential backoff with jitter on Timeout / ConnectionError / 5xx. Any failure returns a safe {speech, actions: []} fallback so the robot says something and moves nothing.
components.parsing: Strips markdown fences, extracts the outermost JSON object, validates against LLMResponse. On validation failure it salvages only the speech field and drops all actions.

components.name: PiperTTS
components.responsibility: Render WAV in memory, then route it. Phone camera in use and phone connected -> emit over SocketIO to the phone speaker; otherwise pipe to aplay on the laptop, with automatic fallback if the phone path throws.
components.concurrency: non-blocking by default via a daemon thread; a non-blocking lock drops overlapping utterances instead of queueing them. Live subprocesses are tracked in a WeakSet and terminated at shutdown.

components.name: WebServer (Flask-SocketIO)
components.responsibility: The phone bridge. Authenticated SocketIO handshake, phone mic audio in, sensors in, TTS audio out, state broadcast out, MJPEG stream, REST commands, embedded browser dashboard.
components.concurrency: daemon thread 'web-server' plus a supervised 'state-pusher' thread
hardening: Bearer token on every REST route, compared with hmac.compare_digest
Missing JARVIS_SECRET_KEY returns 503 and refuses to start the server; it never silently runs open
SocketIO connect handler returns False on a bad or missing token
CORS reflected only for origins in the ALLOWED_ORIGINS list
Payload caps: 1 MB body on /command, 512 KB audio frame, 8 KB sensor JSON
Move duration clamped to [0.1, MOVE_MAX_DURATION_S]; a single shared timer is cancelled and replaced so repeated moves cannot leak threads
components.efficiency: Frames are only JPEG-encoded when a browser or app client is actually attached.

components.name: REST blueprint
components.responsibility: Secondary /api/robot/* surface registered onto the Flask app after the server thread comes up (polled up to 5 s). Same Bearer auth, Pydantic-validated body.

components.name: RobotComms
components.topology: The laptop is the TCP server on :9999; the ESP32 dials in as a client.
components.responsibility: Single-byte command transport plus the geometry-to-command translation helpers.
hardening: Allow-list at the socket boundary: FBLRS motor plus GOUD arm. Anything else is dropped and logged.
Always uppercased and truncated to one character before send
Duplicate commands are suppressed; the board holds its last state
resilience: TCP_NODELAY and 50 ms send timeout so the CV loop never stalls on a dead link
select() before every write; a broken pipe clears the client and schedules reconnect
Exponential backoff with jitter from ESP32_RECONNECT_BASE_S 1 s to ESP32_RECONNECT_MAX_S 30 s
Initial connect runs on a background thread so the loop starts with no hardware present

components.name: Flutter app (jarvis_app)
components.responsibility: Four screens (home, control, vision, settings) over a Provider-held SocketService. Streams mic PCM16 up, plays TTS WAV down, publishes IMU and GPS, sends mode and move commands, renders the MJPEG feed.
components.auth: Host and token persist in SharedPreferences and are sent both as SocketIO auth payload and query fallback.

components.name: Embedded browser dashboard
components.responsibility: Zero-dependency fallback UI served at /. Polls /status every second, posts move and mode commands. Reads its bearer token from localStorage.

components.name: ESP32 motor controller
components.responsibility: Join Wi-Fi, dial the brain on TCP :9999, recv() one byte at a time, drive the pins. It makes no decisions.
components.pwm: LEDC low-speed mode, 1 kHz, 8-bit. SPEED_NORMAL 200, SPEED_TURN 180.
failsafe: Socket disconnect (recv <= 0) -> motor_stop() then reconnect after 500 ms
Connect failure -> motor_stop() then retry after 1 s

runtime_threads.name: main
runtime_threads.role: CV loop, 20 fps cap, cv2 window and hotkeys

runtime_threads.name: state-pusher
runtime_threads.role: emit state_update to the phone on a 100 ms tick while connected

runtime_threads.name: esp32-initial-connect
runtime_threads.role: first accept() poll so startup is not blocked on hardware

runtime_threads.name: vla-warmup / vla inference

runtime_threads.name: move stop timer

modes.description: Default and safe state. Also the forced state when the camera is unavailable or an emergency keyword is heard.
Line following via the MobileNetV2 classifier.
YOLOv8n person tracking with EMA smoothing and safe-distance logic. Rotates right to search when nobody is visible.

modes.command: first move action from the last VLA response

modes.description: CV loop stops deciding; the app, the dashboard or a timed queue move owns the motors.
Accepted as an action type and settable via the web bridge, but the CV loop has no GOTO branch. Falls through to the unknown-mode guard and stops.

esp32_tcp.transport: TCP, laptop listens on :9999, ESP32 connects out
esp32_tcp.payload: one ASCII byte per command, no framing, no ack

commands.S: stop, duty 0 and all direction pins low

socketio.auth: token in the handshake auth dict, query param fallback; rejected connections return False

phone_to_laptop.limit: 512 KB per frame, queue 400 deep with drop-oldest

phone_to_laptop.effect: skip the wake word for one cycle
same handler as REST /command, replies with command_ack

laptop_to_phone.cadence: 100 ms tick while the phone is connected

laptop_to_phone.payload: raw WAV bytes for the phone speaker

action_schema.validator: pydantic, discriminated union on 'type', model LLMResponse{speech, actions[]}
action_schema.enforcement: Every model output, text or vision, is validated before it can touch the queue. A validation failure drops all actions and keeps only the speech.

fields.value: LFR | HUMAN_TRACK | VLA | GOTO | MANUAL | IDLE

data_flows.rate: 20 fps cap, buffer size 1, MJPG fourcc for low latency

data_flows.payload: frame copy on a worker thread

data_flows.rate: every loop iteration, de-duplicated at the socket

data_flows.note: encoded only when a client is attached

data_flows.payload: mic PCM16, IMU, GPS, commands, force_listen
validated action tokens with correlation id

data_flows.when: phone camera in use and phone connected

controls.control: JARVIS_SECRET_KEY and all paths come from .env, which is git-ignored. Nothing is hardcoded in Python.
A missing secret returns 503 and stops the web server from starting. Absence of config is never treated as permission.
hmac.compare_digest on every bearer and handshake token check.
Pydantic discriminated union validates every model action before execution; failures drop actions and keep speech only.
Socket boundary accepts only FBLRSGOUD; the board also stops on any unknown byte.
Move duration clamped to [0.1, 5.0] s at both the queue and the web handler, so a model or a client cannot drive indefinitely.
1 MB request body, 512 KB audio frame, 8 KB sensor JSON, bounded queues with drop-oldest.
flask-limiter, 5 commands per second per address.
Origins reflected only from ALLOWED_ORIGINS; SocketIO uses the same list.
RLock plus copy.deepcopy on every dict getter and on snapshot(); no mutable reference escapes.
Emergency keywords (stop, halt, freeze, abort, emergency, cancel) short-circuit before the LLM, clear the queue and force IDLE.

findings.detail: Wi-Fi SSID, Wi-Fi password and the brain server IP are hardcoded as string literals in a tracked source file. The credentials are in git history.
findings.fix: Move them to sdkconfig / Kconfig or NVS provisioning and rotate the Wi-Fi password.

findings.detail: The motor TCP port accepts the first client that connects, with no authentication. Anyone on the LAN can drive the robot.
findings.fix: Pre-shared key handshake on accept, or bind to a dedicated interface.

findings.detail: pvporcupine is still declared and documented, but the live wake word engine is openWakeWord.
findings.fix: Drop pvporcupine and correct the README and CLAUDE.md.

required.purpose: bearer token for REST and the SocketIO handshake

voice.validated: must exist and be executable when voice is enabled

failure_modes.handling: CameraUnavailable caught, mode forced IDLE, voice and manual control keep working
send() returns False, background reconnect with jittered backoff up to 30 s; the CV loop never blocks
Board sees recv <= 0 and stops the motors before reconnecting; the laptop clears the client and schedules reconnect
Retry with backoff, then a safe fallback response with zero actions; startup health check warns but does not abort

failure_modes.failure: Model emits malformed or hostile JSON
failure_modes.handling: Pydantic rejects it, actions are dropped, only speech survives
ThreadSupervisor restarts it, up to 10 times in 60 s, then marks it degraded
Bounded at 128 with drop-oldest and a loud log line
failure_modes.blast_radius: oldest actions lost, no memory growth

failure_modes.handling: Queue bounded at 400 chunks, drop-oldest, oversize frames rejected with audio_error
Falls back to a pygame preview window
finally block sends S, releases the camera, stops the supervisor, closes sockets, terminates TTS subprocesses

suites.covers: RobotState locking, RobotComms translation and allow-list, utils
web server routes, auth, payload handling
ESP32 disconnect, Ollama retry, payload bombs, queue exhaustion, missing devices, thread supervisor, logging setup

deployment.backend: uv sync, then uv run python -m backend.main. Dev flags: --no-socket, --no-web, --laptop, --no-wake-word (spacebar PTT).
deployment.mobile_app: cd jarvis_app && flutter pub get && flutter build apk --debug
deployment.firmware: cd backend/esp32 && idf.py set-target esp32 && idf.py flash monitor
deployment.containers: Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml present at the repo root

known_gaps: GOTO mode is accepted by the LLM schema, the queue and the web bridge, but the CV loop has no GOTO branch; it hits the unknown-mode guard and stops.
Arm commands G/O/U/D pass the socket allow-list but main.c has no arm handling; the board treats them as unknown and stops.
HybridLineFollower is ML-only. The OpenCV fallback the name implies is commented out, so a failed model load means LOST rather than degraded steering.
tracker.py hardcodes an absolute local path for the line classifier weights.
WebServer.update_conversation is a no-op kept only for compatibility.
Documentation drift: Porcupine vs openWakeWord, and the README shows a 300 ms state broadcast where the code ticks at 100 ms.
